title: Adam Hamilton wins in Kansas to become state’s first Democrat in Senate since 1932
summary: Pastor clinches victory over incumbent Roger Marshall in state that emerged as unexpected battleground this year

blocks.text: Adam Hamilton has clinched a historic victory in the US Senate race in Kansas, fueling the country’s Democratic takeover of Congress as voters in key battleground states expressed frustration with Donald Trump. It’s the first time a Democrat has been elected to represent Kansas in the Senate since 1932.

With his victory speech, Hamilton, a longtime pastor, transformed a crowded hotel ballroom into his own congregation, his podium into a pulpit. Speaking at a hotel in Overland Park, he recited Bible passages and the parable of Good Samaritan in his address.

“Do unto others as you’d have them do unto you,” he said, citing Matthew 7:12 in the Bible that’s more commonly known as “the golden rule”. “What does it look like in Washington if they actually did that? How would our policies and our politics change if we treated people this way?”

Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, 66, who served as US senator for the state since 2021 and was elected to the US House of Representatives for two terms. But it was Marshall’s work as an obstetrician that factored heavily into his re-election campaign, after the New York Times reported that he had sued hundreds of his patients for unpaid bills, including dozens who were arrested after missing their court dates.

Kansas emerged as an unexpected battleground this year. The closely watched Cook Political Report rated the race as a toss-up, noting it was one of several agriculture-heavy areas to be hit hard by high fuel and fertilizer prices because of Trump’s war on Iran.
Hamilton ultimately won over Marshall with 51.1% of the vote, according to the AP’s tally as of early Wednesday morning.

Democratic pastor Hamilton, 62, leads the largest United Methodist congregation in the country, United Methodist Church of the Resurrection based in the Kansas City area. He calls himself an “independent-minded Democrat” and had argued Kansas would benefit from having one US senator from each party. The state’s other seat is held by Republican Jerry Moran.
Hamilton, who has frequently said that decency was on the ballot, pledged to become “Jerry Moran’s best friend” and bring members of both parties together to “solve problems, like it used to be”.
“In deeply red Kansas, the heart of America, I want us to model what it looks like when thoughtful people actually work together to solve problems, instead of slinging mud at each other,” he said.

Trump won Kansas handily in 2024, and sought to inspire Republican turnout by hosting rallies in the state leading up to election day. But Marshall’s liabilities, particularly the medical billing scandal, and Hamilton’s attempt at a pragmatic bipartisan appeal helped tighten the race this year. Several of the counties Marshall won in 2020 flipped for Hamilton this year, according to AP election data, and even the counties he did win were by much narrower margins than in his last election.

Hamilton, who branded himself as a centrist with the slogan, “leading from the middle”, joined several other “prairie populists” this year to win over Republican strongholds by leaning on populist messaging and vowing to stand up to corruption and corporate interests.

Hamilton also successfully tapped into voter concerns about the high cost of living, as did many other successful Democrats in tight races. In a brief interview with the Guardian on Tuesday morning, Hamilton said his first priority to lower costs for Kansans would be to end the war in Iran, which have nearly doubled diesel and fertilizer prices for the thousands of farmers in the state. Kansas is about 88% farmland, and roughly one in five of its residents work in the agriculture industry, according to the state’s department of agriculture.

Hamilton told voters during the campaign that he would be more accessible to them than Marshall has been in office. Marshall, notably, last held an open town hall with his constituents in early 2025, when he left the town hall after facing pointed questions. (Marshall has said the town halls became “non-productive and dangerous”.)
It’s not unheard of for Kansas to elect Democrats to statewide roles. Laura Kelly, the state’s outgoing governor, is a Democrat and has held the governorship since 2019.

After the results were called, Jeff Burgess, an attendee at Hamilton’s watch party, said no other candidate had come closer to representing his own beliefs than Hamilton. A 49-year-old small business owner from Lawrence, he said he appreciated Hamilton’s ability to weigh difficult and conflicting issues, and was hopeful that Kansan legislators would better represent the interests of their constituents.

“Hamilton is a reasonable person. He does not claim to know all the answers for all of the complicated things, but he’s reasonable,” he said. “He’s willing to listen. He is not tied to some kind of self-beneficial agenda that’s going to make him rich. He cares about people and what their needs are. He cares about suffering.”

When Hamilton was declared the projected winner by CNN, the crowd at his watch party in Overland Park erupted in a deafening roar. The crowd chanted his name. They wept. They leapt to embrace their neighbors.
A rock band that had been playing covers earlier in the night took up their instruments again. A thumping drumbeat propelled them into their first song following the victory.
“I’m walking on sunshine,” sang the lead singer. “And don’t it feel good!”
